title: When Is the Best Time to Visit Kenya for Safari? It Depends on the Park
meta_title: Best Time to Visit Kenya for Safari, Park by Park
meta_description: The best time to visit Kenya for safari, month by month: dry seasons, the Mara migration, green-season prices and the right month for each park.
excerpt: The best time to visit Kenya for safari is late June to October, but January, February and even the green season have real advantages. Here is how each month and each park compares.
content:
The best time to visit Kenya for a safari is the long dry season from late June to October, when grass is short, animals crowd around water and the Great Migration fills the Masai Mara. January and February are a close second: dry, hot, quieter and cheaper. April and May, the long rains, are the wettest months.

That headline answer is true, but it hides a lot. Kenya has two rainy seasons, two dry seasons and parks that behave very differently from one another, so the best time to visit Kenya for Amboseli is not always the right month for the Mara, Samburu or the coast. This guide breaks the year down month by month and park by park, shows what each season does to prices, and helps you match the calendar to the trip you actually want.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Quick Facts

  • Best time to visit Kenya: Late June to October (long dry season)
  • Great Migration: Usually July to October in the Masai Mara, river crossings most likely late July to September
  • Second dry season: Mid-December to early March: hot, green, fewer vehicles
  • Long rains: Roughly late March to May, heaviest in April
  • Short rains: Roughly late October to early December, mostly afternoon showers
  • Mara reserve fee: US$100 per adult per day January-June, US$200 July-December (checked October 2026)
  • Cheapest months: April, May and early June

When Is the Best Time to Visit Kenya for a Safari?

The best time to visit Kenya for a safari, for most first-time visitors, is July to October. These months are dry, the vegetation thins out, wildlife is easy to find around rivers and waterholes, and the migration herds are usually in the Masai Mara. The trade-off is peak prices and more vehicles at sightings.

Kenya sits on the equator, so the best time to visit Kenya is decided by rain rather than temperature. Daytime temperatures in the main safari parks stay warm all year, while Nairobi and the highlands, at well over 1,500 metres, have chilly mornings in June, July and August. Pack a fleece for early game drives whatever month you travel.

Why the dry season makes game viewing easier

In the dry months, surface water disappears from the plains and animals have to drink at permanent rivers, swamps and waterholes. That concentrates elephants, buffalo and antelope in predictable places, and the predators follow. Shorter grass also means you can actually see a lion lying 50 metres from the track, which is far harder in May when the grass stands waist high. That, more than anything, is why the dry season is the best time to visit Kenya for big game.

Is the dry season the same across Kenya?

Not quite. The Masai Mara and the southern parks follow the classic pattern of long rains in April and May and short rains around November. The dry north around Samburu gets less rain overall and stays good for much of the year, while the coast has its own humid rhythm, with its heaviest rain usually from April to June. That is why the best time to visit Kenya depends partly on your route, and why a mixed itinerary can work in more months than you might expect.

Kenya's Safari Seasons Month by Month

Kenya's safari year splits into four parts: the long dry season (late June to October), the short rains (around November), the short dry season (mid-December to early March) and the long rains (late March to May). The table sums up the best time to visit Kenya month by month.

MonthWeatherWildlife and parksCrowds and prices
JanuaryHot and mostly dry after the short rainsExcellent across the country; green plains, young animals, migrant birdsBusy in the first week, then quieter; Mara fee at the lower rate
FebruaryDriest and hottest stretch of the first half of the yearVery good everywhere; animals cluster at water in Samburu, Tsavo and AmboseliGood value and fewer vehicles
MarchHeat and humidity build; rains often start late in the monthStill good early on; clouds return over KilimanjaroPrices start to drop
AprilLong rains at their heaviestLush scenery, birds, very few visitors; some tracks muddyLowest prices; some seasonal camps close
MayLong rains continue, easing towards the endGreen and quiet; drives can be cut short by stormsLow season rates
JuneRains end; cool mornings in the highlandsGrass starts to dry; good value before the migration crowdsShoulder season; still the lower Mara fee
JulyDry and cool, especially around NairobiMigration herds usually arrive in the Masai MaraHigh season starts; Mara fee doubles from 1 July
AugustDry, clear and coolPeak migration and the best odds of river crossingsBusiest and dearest month; book months ahead
SeptemberDry and warmingHerds still in the Mara; excellent game everywhereVery busy, a little calmer late in the month
OctoberDry, hot; showers may appear late in the monthMigration thinning but often still present; birds start arrivingHigh season fees, slightly lighter crowds
NovemberShort rains, usually as afternoon showersGreen and fresh, migrant birds in full numbersGood shoulder-season deals
DecemberShowers ease through the monthYoung animals, green parks; herds mostly back in TanzaniaQuiet early on, peak over Christmas and New Year

Treat this calendar of the best time to visit Kenya as a guide rather than a promise. Rains can start a fortnight early or late, and the Kenya Meteorological Department publishes seasonal forecasts ahead of each rainy season that are worth a look before you fix dates. If your heart is set on a particular month, our Kenya safari in January guide and December safari guide go into far more detail.

When Is the Great Migration in the Masai Mara?

The Great Migration usually crosses from Tanzania's Serengeti into Kenya's Masai Mara in July and stays until about October. Mara River crossings, the dramatic part most people want to see, are most likely from late July to September, although herds can cross at any point in that window and sometimes back and forth several times.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

For many travellers this is the best time to visit Kenya, but the exact timing depends on when the rains fall in the Serengeti, so no one can promise a crossing on a given day. What you can control is time: three or four nights in the Mara gives you whole days to wait by the river. Our 7-day Mara river crossing safari is built around exactly that, with three nights in the reserve. For where the herds are in every other month, see our Great Migration month-by-month guide.

Is the Masai Mara worth visiting outside the migration?

Yes. The Mara has resident lions, leopards, cheetahs, elephants and plains game all year, and from November to June you share sightings with far fewer vehicles. The reserve fee also halves between January and June, so for value seekers the best time to visit Kenya's most famous reserve may be outside the migration. Our Masai Mara seasons guide covers the reserve itself month by month, including the green season.

Which Months Suit Each Kenyan Park?

The best time to visit Kenya depends on which parks are on your list, because each has its own sweet spot. Amboseli and Tsavo shine in the dry months, Samburu is reliable for most of the year, Lake Nakuru and Naivasha work well in every season, and the coast is happiest outside April to June.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Amboseli and Tsavo

For Amboseli, the best time to visit Kenya is June to October and again from January to early March, when elephants walk out of the dust to drink and feed at the swamps. Kilimanjaro is most often visible at dawn and dusk, and clear days are more common in the dry seasons. Tsavo East and Tsavo West follow a similar pattern; in the dry months the red-dust elephants concentrate around the Galana River, the Mzima Springs area and waterholes. Our Amboseli lodges guide helps you choose where to stay.

Samburu, Meru and Laikipia

In the north, the best time to visit Kenya is wider: Samburu is semi-arid, so it stays rewarding for much of the year and is especially good from June to October and January to March, when wildlife lines the Ewaso Ng'iro River. This is where you find the northern specials: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, gerenuk and Beisa oryx. Meru, greener and much quieter, is best in the same dry windows. If you are weighing the north against the Mara, our Samburu vs Masai Mara comparison sets out the trade-offs.

Lake Nakuru, Naivasha and the Rift Valley

The Rift Valley lakes are year-round destinations. Lake Nakuru's rhinos and Naivasha's boat rides and hippos do not depend on the season, which makes these parks a good stop if the best time to visit Kenya for you falls during the rains. Flamingo numbers on the soda lakes rise and fall with water levels and are hard to predict, so treat big flocks as a bonus rather than the reason to go.

The Kenya coast for bush and beach

Diani, Watamu and Lamu are warm all year, but the best time to visit Kenya for bush and beach is outside the coast's wettest months. The calmest, driest beach weather usually falls from late December to March and again from July to October, which fits neatly around a dry-season safari. April to June is the coast's wettest and most humid period, and some beach hotels close or cut services then.

Is the Green Season a Good Time for a Kenya Safari?

The green season can be an excellent time for a Kenya safari if you value space and price over perfect weather. From April to early June and again in November, the parks are lush, lodges offer lower rates, and you will often have sightings to yourself. Rain usually falls in heavy bursts, not all day.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Not everyone will find the green season the best time to visit Kenya. The honest downsides: some black-cotton-soil tracks in the Mara and Amboseli become slippery, a number of seasonal camps close for part of April and May, and taller grass makes cats harder to spot. A good driver-guide and a 4x4 Land Cruiser make a real difference in these months. Birders, on the other hand, love the period from about October to March, when migrants from Europe and Asia join Kenya's resident species; our 16-day Kenya migrant birding safari is timed for those months.

Best time to visit Kenya on a budget

If cost matters most, the best time to visit Kenya on a budget is April to mid-June, followed by November and the first half of December. Park fees are the one cost you cannot negotiate, and the season changes them in the Mara but not in the KWS parks.

FeeJanuary-JuneJuly-December
Masai Mara National Reserve, non-resident adult per dayUS$100US$200
Amboseli or Lake Nakuru, non-resident adult per 24 hoursUS$90US$90
Nairobi, Tsavo East or Tsavo West, non-resident adult per 24 hoursUS$80US$80

The KWS rates come from the Kenya Wildlife Service fee regulations in force since 1 October 2025, and the Mara rates are set by Narok County (all checked October 2026). Fees change, so confirm them before you book, whatever you decide is the best time to visit Kenya. Our Kenya park fees guide lists every park, and our Kenya safari cost breakdown shows how the season changes total trip prices.

Which Month Fits Your Kind of Trip?

The best time to visit Kenya depends on what you want most from the trip. Migration seekers should aim for August or September, value hunters for February or June, birders for November to March, and families for the July-August school holidays, accepting peak prices. Honeymooners often pair a dry-season safari with the coast.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

First safari

For a first trip, the best time to visit Kenya is late June or early July and the second half of September are the sweet spots: dry-season game viewing, a strong chance of migration herds and slightly fewer vehicles than in August. A week with Amboseli, Lake Nakuru or Naivasha and three nights in the Mara covers the classic Kenya experience.

Photographers

For photographers, the best time to visit Kenya is often the short dry season from January to early March. The air is cleaner after the short rains, the light is softer, there is green grass under the animals and many herbivores have young. August gives the drama of river crossings but also the dust and the crowds.

Climbers

If you want to add Mount Kenya, the most settled climbing weather is usually January to February and late June to early October, the same dry windows that make the best time to visit Kenya for a safari. See our mountain climbing packages to combine a climb with a safari.

Insider Tips

  • Book August early: Mara camps near the river fill six to twelve months ahead for August
  • Use the fee switch: Late June gives dry-season viewing at the lower Mara fee, which rises on 1 July
  • Fly in the rains: In April and May, a short flight to the Mara avoids muddy roads and saves a day
  • Think regionally: If the Mara is busy, Samburu, Meru or a private conservancy can be far quieter
  • Pack layers: Mornings can be cold in open vehicles from June to August
  • Allow time: Three nights in one place beats one night in three places in any season

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best month to visit Kenya for a safari?

The best time to visit Kenya for a safari is usually August or September for the Great Migration in the Masai Mara, and February for dry, quiet parks at lower prices. Both months bring short grass and animals gathered near water. July and October are close behind, while April and May are the wettest.

Which months should I avoid for a Kenya safari?

Most travellers avoid April and May, the heart of Kenya's long rains, when tracks turn muddy, some seasonal camps close and afternoon storms are frequent. It is not a lost season, though: lodges cut rates, the parks are green and empty, and morning drives are often dry. Early November can also bring heavy showers with the short rains.

When is the Great Migration in Kenya?

The Great Migration usually reaches Kenya's Masai Mara in July and stays until about October, with Mara River crossings most likely from late July to September. The timing shifts each year with the rains in Tanzania, so herds can arrive early or late. If the migration is your goal, this is the best time to visit Kenya, and three or more nights in the Mara give you the best chance of seeing a crossing.

Is it cheaper to go on safari in Kenya in the low season?

Yes. If price matters, the low season is the best time to visit Kenya. The Masai Mara reserve fee falls from US$200 to US$100 per adult per day between January and June (checked October 2026), and many lodges offer lower green-season rates from April to June. KWS park fees, such as Amboseli's US$90, stay the same all year.

Is Kenya good for a safari in December?

Kenya is good for a safari in December. The short rains usually ease during the month, the parks are green, and many young animals are around, though the herds of the Great Migration have mostly moved back to Tanzania. Christmas and New Year are busy and priced as peak, so book camps and flights early.

Final Thoughts

The best time to visit Kenya for most people is the dry season from late June to October, with January and February as a quieter, cheaper alternative. The green season suits travellers who prefer empty parks and lower prices, and Kenya's variety means there is a good park for almost any month.

Once you know the best time to visit Kenya for your own trip, the rest of the plan falls into place: which parks to pair, how many nights in each and whether to drive or fly. Send us your dates and we will tell you honestly what that month looks like.
